body.statement: After matching the common selector-gated syntax, \[\Theta_H=\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^{+})\cap\{\theta:\operatorname{supp}_{p_\theta}(S)=H,\ p_\theta(c)>0\ \text{ for every }c\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^{+})\}\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^{+}).\] The inclusion is strict whenever the published class permits either positive mass at some selector value outside \(H\) or a structural-model law on a boundary admissible cell. Moreover, \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\subseteq\Theta_H^2\subseteq\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{LGS}}(G^{+})^2\). In general \(\mathcal W_{\mathrm{LGS}}^{(5)}\not\subseteq\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\): a pair allowed by the published failure guarantee that assigns mass outside \(H\), violates an admissible-cell interior inequality, or equates only the branch inputs rather than every coordinate of \(O_H\) fails the defining predicate of \(\mathcal W_H^{\mathrm{global}}\). Hence a failure witness valid over the larger published class does not establish nonidentification on the fixed-support subclass; the new negative branch must verify exact support and full all-cell equality directly.
body.justification: This inclusion comparison isolates the logical obstruction to importing a larger-class branchwise witness into the fixed-support completeness theorem.
body.gap: Theorem 5 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser certifies specified failure constructions in its published model, but it does not type every output as an exact-\(H\), full-joint-law twin in the restricted-support interior subclass.
body.consumer: Reviewers and implementers can distinguish a legal fixed-support nonidentification certificate from a witness that silently adds a context or preserves only part of the supplied joint table.
